text: You can get out of bed, walk through the house, and open the front door, while you're still asleep.
This is sleepwalking. It starts in deep sleep, the slow-wave stage, usually in the first third of the night.
Normally, the whole brain sleeps together. In a sleepwalker, it splits.
Areas that control movement wake up,
while areas that handle judgment and awareness stay in deep sleep.
So the body walks, often with eyes open, but no one is really in charge. Most people remember little or nothing.
It's most common in kids. About five percent of children sleepwalk in a year, compared with one and a half percent of adults.

text: It often runs in families, and lack of sleep, stress, fever, or some medicines can trigger it.
If you find someone sleepwalking, you don't need to wake them. Gently guide them back to bed.
